simple.meaning: חָצִיר (châtsîyr) is a Hebrew word meaning “a court or abode.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.

definitions.full: H2681. chatsir I. חָצִיר noun [masculine] settled abode or haunt (|| form of חָצֵר above , or text error for it); — יַעֲנָה לִבְנוֺת חָצִיר תַנִּים נְוֵה Isa 34:13 a dwelling of jackals (and) a hunt for ostriches ; also וָגֹ֑מֶא לְקָנֶה חָצִיר רִבְצָהּ תַנִּים בִּנְוֵת 35:7 an abode, home, of reeds and rushes (so Che Di Du and others; others put this under II. חָצִיר ); Che Du think the see mutilated, and would emend this line according to 34:13 .
